article_title: Doing One's Energy Homework in the '80s
brief_extract:
Doing One's Energy Homework in the '80s

From its earliest days in the 1920's, the EAW has been providing a unique service of public education, information and advice for all users of electricity in the home. Whilst the organisation has always been supported generously, though not entirely, by various sectors of the British electrical industry, the EAW's 200-plus branches have remained determinedly self-supporting and staunchly independent. Likewise, the organisation's National Executive Committee, composed of members elected by the membership, has run the affairs of the Association for 56 years, free of any form of pressure or interference.

brief_context: The formation of the world's first standards body occurred here.
brief_extract: The logic of, and need for, standardisation in commerce and industry is nowadays universally accepted and the existence of standards is often taken for granted. Yet nationally agreed standards and the formation in Britain of the world's first standards body — now known as British Standards Institution — did not come about until the beginning of the present century. BSI is the national organisation for preparing standards which lays down the technical requirements that a material, product or procedure must satisfy to be fit for its purpose.

A leading personality in this select band of women is Dr Elizabeth Laverick, C.Eng., FIEE, FInstP, with an outstanding record of achievements. In 1946 she became the first woman PhD in Physics at Durham University. She was possibly the first Woman Technical Director of a large electronics company and she has been Deputy Secretary of the IEE since 1970, the first woman engineer to hold this top position.

brief_context: Where Laverick conducted early career research during the war.
brief_extract: Her physics master convinced her that she should turn to physics - her second best subject and one, of course, closely associated with mathematics. This was during the war and although she could only do a small amount of research work it was enough to sow the seeds of her future career.

brief_context: Mentioned in relation to the Army's success in jungle war.
